name: Temiar
catalog_quote: Word-stress is not significant, falling regularly on the final syllable. Sentence-stress forms part of the suprasegmental accentual system and is accordingly not discussed here, except insofar as it affects allomorphic alternations.

sources.citation: Matisoff, James A. 2003. Aslian: Mon-Khmer of the Malay Peninsula. Mon-Khmer Studies 33: 1-58 (with embedded comments by G. Benjamin).
sources.quote: 'Sesquisyllabic forms consist of a "major" syllable with fully-stressed vowel, preceded by a "minor" syllable with predictable vocalism (e.g. Temiar ... )'; 'Truly disyllabic words have non-predictable vowels in their non-final syllables. In these cases, even if the non-final vowel is unstressed (e.g. "monitor lizard" Semai ..., Temiar kabug, Jah Hut kabok) ...'; 'Disyllabic compounds with unreduced though unstressed vowels also occur (e.g. Temiar diŋ-rab "shelter").' I.e. stress on the final (major) syllable, non-final syllables unstressed, Temiar cited explicitly.

sources.citation: Diffloth, Gérard. 1976. Minor-syllable vocalism in Senoic languages. In Jenner, Thompson & Starosta (eds), Austroasiatic Studies I, 229-247. Honolulu: University Press of Hawaii.
sources.quote: Frames Senoic (incl. Temiar) words as final 'major' syllable plus preceding 'minor' syllables; anticipatory minor vowels described as 'a short, unaccented' copy of the major vowel. No explicit statement of Temiar word-stress location in the pages read.
